To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the joint selling of television rights of professional football clubs can have an anticompetitive effect on the market for the distribution of media rights.

the new enforcement regime introduced by Regulation 1/2013, the decentralisation of enforcement and the new tool of commitments, are an improvement of European competition law enforcement, that however bear risks of inconsistent application of competition law within the EU.

the new competition law enforcement regime under Regulation 1/2013 has introduced a new tool to react to anticompetitive practices on the media market and that the Commission and NCAS have used this tool in a different manner, which bears risks of inconsistent policy and application.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question, how competition authorities in the EU should deal with the joint selling of television rights and especially how they should react to the constant change on media markets, which is caused by the digitalisation of media content and the increasing competition of the internet platforms.

the question of whether a joint selling of media rights of football clubs is compatible with the EU competition rules and how the new enforcement regime and the tool of commitment decisions will affect the application of competition policy in the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Commission and the national authorities have to be very cautious in the future when dealing with the joint sale.
the Commission and NCs have different approaches to the joint sale of football media rights and the application of Art. 101 and 102 TFEU.

, despite the fact that the joint sale of football media rights is an issue that needs to be dealt with by the European competition authorities, the European Commission and the NCsAs should be more cautious in the future, to ensure that competition law and policy are applied consistently and uniformly throughout the EU.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the joint sale of TV rights of football leagues is an issue of competition law, but that it is not a matter of antitrust law.
the joint sale of TV rights is a complex matter and that competition law enforcements need to be careful in their assessment of the joint sale of football media rights.

the thesis will show that competition law enforcement is a complex and dynamic matter and that the new enforcement regime introduced by Regulation 1/203 is still in its early days and needs time to develop.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is necessary for the European Commission and national authorities alike to keep in mind the uniform application of competition law in the EU.
the new enforcement regime under Regulation 1/2013 and especially the possibility to accept commitments, provide a flexible and effective tool to target anticompetitive practices.
it is necessary, to take the new enforcement regime and especially its new tools and the margin of discretion of competition authorities seriously.
